svg.title: Fig. 93 — y = x · sin(1/x) between the lines y = ±x
svg.desc: Redrawn from Robert C. Yates, A Handbook on Curves and Their Properties (1947), Fig. 93, page 101. Section: discontinuous.

g.data-text: The axes and the bounding lines y = x and y = −x (|x · sin(1/x)| ≤ |x|), dashed.

The curve: the same oscillation on both sides (the function is even). Put u = 1/x: the points (1/u, sin(u)/u) touch the lines y = ±x at the points where sin(1/x) = ±1, x = 2/((2m + 1)π), the waves crowd towards the origin, and the curve stays between y = −1 and y = 1.
The limit at x = 0 is 0, so the open point at the origin is removable. For large |x| the curve approaches the line y = 1 (dashed).
